description: A Christmas special leads into the 2025 run, where rebuses, hidden occupations, date codes, compound words and exact visual counting dominate, followed by a delayed November episode and a football-themed Soccer Aid special.

s04e00.description: The Boxing Day special uses snowmen, advent calendars and other Christmas imagery, including a spot-the-difference puzzle whose wording around a pair of legs proves unexpectedly contentious. The final letter puzzle can first suggest LISTEN before rearrangement reveals the intended festive answer: TINSEL.

s04e01.description: A crossword clue yields EXPLORE, clothing pictures hide scarf and boots, and arranging playing cards alphabetically ends on the Two of Spades. The final simply asks for the dots in the written question itself, with seventeen hiding in plain sight.

s04e02.description: A maze, a shape-counting picture and a word build that combines S, CRAB and BLE lead to SCRABBLE. Another chain hides animal names across PHEASANT, TORTOISE and LION before a month-number puzzle turns calendar familiarity into a code.

s04e03.description: STUN, DUST and SNUB are reversed, everyday objects are sorted alphabetically and ELECTORAL SYSTEM is rearranged into SCARLETT MOSELEY. A phone-style layout hides DON'T CRY OVER SPILT MILK, making the episode particularly fond of text that must be reorganised rather than read normally.

s04e04.description: A bridge-word puzzle links HANDLEBAR, BARBELL and related compounds before the final rebus shows a sprained ankle alongside an insult. The literal combination is ADDING INSULT TO INJURY, a familiar phrase rebuilt from two visual clues.

s04e05.description: RECTANGLE wins a largest-shape question by letter count rather than area, a bungalow-light puzzle removes imagined staircases and a Macbeth clue advances through sixty days. The final diary code resolves to the occupation FLORIST.

s04e06.description: MARK links QUESTION, BOOK and TRADE, while the password PURPLE PARROT PAULA rewards exact repetition. TEN is found in nine matchsticks, PUPPY contains UP and later clues range from Keir Starmer picture wordplay to PENELOPE and CANDY.

s04e07.description: LEM over ADE forms LEMONADE, butterfly symmetry and FIGHT OR FLIGHT give way to CONVERSATION becoming CONSERVATION. The final asks for the lowest number equal to ten times the number of letters in its written name, producing FIFTY.

s04e08.description: ABRACADABRA is read backwards, CAKE is hidden through holes and ADD becomes part of HADDOCK. Country names supply missing letters and a tongue-twister is counted before a medicine schedule reveals the required start date: 26 March.

s04e09.description: Batman imagery, a self-referential sentence and medal ordering lead to a date-indexing clue that spells FARMER. The final uses words such as TEXT, TOXIN and EXIT to expose a repeated letter-position rule rather than a conventional vocabulary link.

s04e10.description: MICE is tested as an irregular plural, EVIL, VILE, VEIL and LIVE are rearranged, and BUMBLEBEE is examined alphabetically. The Hokey Cokey and WHAT GOES UP MUST COME DOWN appear before the final occupation resolves to FISHMONGER.

s04e11.description: Bats and mice, football's Red Zone and a central-letter puzzle lead into eggs, NEEDLE IN A HAYSTACK and transformations such as WORDS to SWORD and END to DEN. The final four-digit PIN is 1489.

s04e12.description: A helicopter rebus, alphabetical letters in BREAD and a zebra crossing precede consonant-point counting and repeated Hs in Happy Birthday. The last puzzle removes rhyming pairs until the surviving answer is HEAD.

s04e13.description: RAGE becomes SAGE, orchestra sections divide into strings, brass and wind, and later clues use SPRING, MURMUR, CACTUS and SCISSORS. The final finds SEA as the common prefix for son, ted, food, sick, bed and side.

s04e14.description: MANGO appears through magnets, HOME is built from a shape and CONTESTANT is assembled from smaller clues. CUB becomes CUBE, H to O gives WATER and a square-root date points to April before the final sequence settles on 12345.

s04e15.description: Spoons, forks and knives start the visual counting, while PAN, PIN and PEN are compared with PUN and PORCUPINE must fit a grid. A COWS rhyme trap and 999 plus 1000 plus 1001 appear before SEA-like word completion yields TEA.

s04e16.description: Number and word puzzles build toward a final country clue in which the digits must be read as two-digit letter positions rather than individually. Once the numbers are paired correctly, the apparently impossible code resolves into a country name.

s04e17.description: The Soccer Aid special uses football throughout: Liverpool and Arsenal goals become holes, LONE MISSILE rearranges to LIONEL MESSI and bicycle, free and kick form familiar compounds. The final counts appearances of KNOW and IT in the opening of Three Lions.
